ledger.why: who competes: the trials name no villager (no game skill matches these contestants)
a small ('modest') game-scaled tech reward on the constructive outcomes (A2, B1, B2, B3); reputation is told only (rule 7)

intro.name: The trial
intro.text: Two thinkers publicly dispute whether truth comes from reason, experience, tradition, or revelation. Each must fairly restate the other's position before replying.

choices.label: Let the judges name a victor.
Require both debaters to exchange positions.

text_only.reason: narrative: 'experience' is part of the story, not a change the event makes

a1.text: The favored orator wins the audience but loses the scholars, who catch a contradiction.

a2.text: A timid apprentice calmly dismantles a celebrated argument. The defeated master asks to become (apprentice.his/her) student.

text_only.what: tech, food, or appropriate skill experience
text_only.reason: the trial names no villager to gain skill; this trial's constructive success gives tech
narrative: 'celebrated' is part of the story, not a change the event makes

a3.text: The debate becomes personal. The moderator ends it and demands apologies before any prize is awarded.

b1.text: The rivals discover their disagreement rested on two meanings of the same word.

b3.text: Both refuse to concede, but collaborate on a new village school of thought.

p1.text: A judge from the other community praises the winning rival despite pressure from (judge.his/her) own supporters. The crowd slowly applauds.

p2.text: An accusation of favoritism forces the judges to disclose their criteria; the disputed result is upheld, reversed, or declared a tie.

p3.text: Competitors from both communities secretly practice together and publicly acknowledge each other when the results are announced.
